ShortDescription.Value: Million-person cities at full speed: the clock stops waiting for routes, rush hour spreads out, and above a limit you set most people stay home, still counted, working and paying taxes.

Publish.LongDescription:
A city of a million people in the base game runs at about a twentieth of normal speed: vehicles and cims crawl, and a game day takes hours. With Big City Performance the same city runs at about normal speed on the first speed button and faster on the second, on a four-core laptop.
### What it does
**Keep the clock running**
- When the route-finder falls behind, new route requests get more time instead of the game's clock stopping. Emergency services, transit and service vehicles keep the game's own deadlines. - Job hunting and empty taxis search a few at a time while it's busy, everyone in turn. - **Rush hour is spread out**: workers leave across a few minutes instead of all in the same second. Nobody arrives later. - Service coverage is recalculated about once a minute instead of every few seconds. - Below 30 fps the game may run up to twice as many simulation steps per frame, so normal speed stays normal speed.
**Limit the people simulated in detail** (on by default, the limit chosen for you)
- In a city bigger than the limit, that many people are simulated one by one. The rest stay at home, asleep: they keep their homes and jobs, count in the population, earn wages, pay rent and taxes, and still buy from the shops. They just make no trips. - Households take turns, so everyone gets time awake about once every two game days. - At overloaded stops only the first hundred people stay awake; the rest wake in turn as the ones in front board. - **The limit picks itself**: fewer people when the clock falls behind and fewer would help, more when there's room. A slow graphics card alone doesn't lower it. Turn it off to choose the number yourself. - Right after a city loads, the clock waits a moment while the first households go to sleep, instead of everyone asking for routes at once. - **A count in the population box**: while the city is bigger than the limit, the population box at the bottom of the screen also shows how many people are simulated in detail (959,129 | 48k AUTO). Hover it for the details, click it for the settings. - Cities smaller than the limit are not changed at all.
### Measured
The "1 Million Population City" save (about 960,000 people) on a laptop with a four-core processor and an RTX 3050 laptop graphics card:
- Base game: **0.05x** normal speed - First speed button: **about 0.95x**, 17 to 25 fps - Second speed button: **1.4 to 1.6x**
In a city this size the frame rate is mostly the graphics card: the mod simulates a big city faster, it can't draw it faster.
### Settings
In Options, Big City Performance:
- **Keep the clock running** (on) - **Limit the people simulated in detail** (on) - **Choose the limit automatically** (on) - **Most people simulated in detail**, in thousands, for when the automatic limit is off (lower runs faster, higher puts more people on the streets) - **Show it in the population box** (on)
Under **Right now** the page shows what the mod is doing as you play: people simulated in detail out of the population, the game speed reached (1 = normal), and how many wait asleep at crowded stops.
The settings are in English, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian and Chinese.
### Good to know
- Fewer people on the streets of a city over the limit: they're at home. - **Autosave every 10 minutes or more works best.** Every save wakes everyone for a moment, so the save stays ordinary, and they go back to sleep straight after. - Rush hour is gentler, and coverage maps update about once a minute. - **Saves are ordinary saves.** Everyone wakes up before the game saves, and a save loads without the mod. Removing the mod is safe. - Early release: expect rough edges and tell me what you find.
Built for game version **1.6.***.
### Works with other mods
- **Realistic Trips** works. With it and the Stutter Fix, a million-person city ran about a tenth slower in testing. - **Service Coverage Stutter Fix** works, and the two help each other: it makes each coverage update cheaper, this mod runs them less often. On the current game version it shows its own warning popup at start: click Continue. - **Ultra Performance and Simulation Booster** overlaps with this mod. Turn off its Pathfind Queue Unchoker, and its Optimize Parking too: a bug there opens an error popup that pauses the game. - Don't run Ultra Performance and the Stutter Fix together. They clash with each other and show an error popup at every start. - Other mods that change simulation speed or route-finding haven't been tested with it.
### Found a bug?
Click **Report a bug** in Options, Big City Performance, or open an issue on GitHub (link on this page). Add a screenshot and your **BigCityPerformance.log**, from AppData\LocalLow\Colossal Order\Cities Skylines II\Logs. The mod writes a status line there every five minutes, so the log shows how your city was running.
For questions and ideas, the **Discord** button in Options opens this mod's thread in the official Cities: Skylines Discord.
